note: Baseline roster as developed in conversation. Week 1 diffs against this file. scripts/build_report.py copies it to data/sentiment_current.json on first run and updates that file thereafter; this baseline is never overwritten.

fed.name: Fed / Warsh
fed.stance: HIKED 25bps to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, unanimously - the first increase since 2023 - with the dot plot pointing to one more hike this year (median 4.1% end-2026, no change in 2027, cuts in 2028-29)
fed.read: the headwind became an actual tightening. Warsh: inflation has been 'too high for too long' and the FOMC's confidence standard 'has not been satisfied'. Core PCE has run above 3% every month of 2026

roster.name: Yardeni
roster.note: DOWNGRADE: the Street-high bull cut his own target. 7,900 is barely above spot, and he lifted his bearish-scenario odds from 20% to 30%
roster.statement_summary: Cut year-end S&P target 8,400 -> 7,900 and said 'proceed with caution' as the 10y passed 5%; forward P/E assumption 19.8 -> 18.6

roster.name: Wood
roster.note: 'Golden Age' thesis intact: deflationary tech + fiscal push
roster.statement_summary: Q2-26 13F: book up to $15.4bn across 191 names; Tesla/AMD/SpaceX/Tempus/Robinhood ~25% of assets

roster.name: Lee
roster.note: now the loudest bull on the roster, and openly split from Yardeni: reads the hike as REMOVING the pressure for more, and therefore as yields-down, equities-up
roster.statement_summary: Holds S&P above 8,200 by year-end despite the hike, calls it good news for stocks and predicts a historic Q4 rally

roster.name: Siegel
roster.note: constructive but names AI spend, valuations and bond yields as the worries
roster.statement_summary: Weak July payrolls 'overstate' labour-market weakness; still does not expect a bear market

roster.name: Sonders
roster.note: 36m cut to 0: record margin debt, record equity allocations and index concentration are her stated longer-term risks
roster.statement_summary: Rotation backdrop persists and higher yields are biting; investors are 'reluctantly' long via ETF flows and margin debt

roster.name: Druckenmiller
roster.note: GAP WIDENED, not closed: still positioned long megacap tech from Q2, while publicly arguing rates are too LOW and yield suppression is a subsidy to fiscal procrastination. Bearish bonds, long equities, hawkish Fed - pick two
roster.statement_summary: Says rates are already too low and cuts are unnecessary - 'committee members on the Fed who keep saying Fed fund rates are restrictive are just ridiculous'; WSJ op-ed against Treasury long-bond buybacks: if the 30y must trade at 5.5% 'that isn't a crisis, it is an invoice', and the only durable fix is the primary deficit

roster.name: Roubini
roster.note: baseline still 'Goldilocks', but names a more fragile backdrop: Middle East war, AI job-shedding, private-credit stress
roster.statement_summary: Holds the Goldilocks 2026 baseline - tariffs walked back, growth slower, inflation only modestly higher

roster.name: Slok
roster.note: 24m cut to -1: AI capex is running at ~0.85pp of GDP/yr vs 0.5pp in the housing boom, and he warns it 'can unwind at a similar pace'. Bull economy / bear market, with the risk framing moving from stagflation to overheating
roster.statement_summary: AI capex growing nearly twice as fast as the housing boom; rising consumer delinquencies and a widening K-shaped economy on the other side of the ledger

roster.name: El-Erian
roster.note: CALLED IT: in August he said the Treasury buyback was financial engineering that left long rates untouched. The 10y then went through 5%. His new line - interest-rate risk becoming equity and credit risk - is precisely what the HY tile is now showing
roster.statement_summary: Expects the 10y to stay around 5% even if oil falls, citing a structural bond supply/demand imbalance; 'volatility will be a feature, and elevated yields will be a feature for the rest of the year', and 'the big danger' is rate risk turning into equity and credit risk

roster.name: Gross
roster.note: 'No crash, just a forward weave requiring a cane'; bearish long Treasuries on deficits, prefers energy infrastructure and MLPs to exuberant tech
roster.statement_summary: Valuation casts a shadow over 2026; the record rally is at risk of stalling unless AI earnings show up

roster.name: Buffett-Berkshire
roster.note: Deployment continued into Q3 under Abel: ~$39.4bn of equities bought across H1, ~$17bn of it Alphabet via the AI-funding secondary, plus a $6.8bn Taylor Morrison homebuilder acquisition closed in July. Full Q3 13F is not due until November. Cash was still $365.5bn at 30 June, so this is deployment, not capitulation - and note he is buying a homebuilder into the exact housing weakness Burry is shorting
roster.statement_summary: Abel's reversal confirmed: 14-quarter net-selling streak broken with ~$20bn net bought, $4.5bn of buybacks against none in 2025

roster.name: Marks
roster.note: No new memo inside the fortnight, but his private-credit memo is the live thesis: the US private-credit default rate hit a record 6.0% in April (Fitch) and the Proskauer index ran 2.73% in Q1 against 1.84% two quarters earlier - while loan spreads were still tightening. Exactly the 'not being paid for the risk' setup he described
roster.statement_summary: Memo 'What's Going On in Private Credit?' - direct lending's growth, and the issues rapid deployment created

roster.name: Dimon
roster.note: No new statement inside the fortnight, but the tape is validating the April letter and his Norges Bank remarks: private-credit default rates hit a record 6.0% (Fitch, April) and HY OAS has widened 54bps since the last report. 'Credit will perform worse than people expect' is becoming measurable rather than rhetorical - the rhetoric>action gap is closing from the data side, not from him
roster.statement_summary: 'Margin debt is the highest it has ever been', much of it hidden in prime brokerage, ETFs and Treasury-basis trades; says he would not buy the S&P 500 or long-dated Treasuries at today's prices and the market is one bad trade from panic selling

roster.name: Krugman
roster.note: bearish the real economy rather than the index - the gap between the two is his point
roster.statement_summary: August Substack run - 'An Explosion of Misery' (Aug 5) and 'This is your economy on crack (spread)' (Aug 13): the US economy is in worse shape than the tape looks

roster.name: Dalio
roster.note: 24m cut to -4 and conviction to the maximum: he has put a clock on it
roster.statement_summary: Says the US is 'on the brink' and that if the fiscal path does not change a debt shock could hit within two years

roster.name: Rosenberg
roster.note: conviction up: says credit markets are already writing the warning - directly relevant to the HY tripwire
roster.statement_summary: With Richard Bernstein: the AI trade is a bubble, real disposable income is fractionally negative y/y, and ex-AI the four-quarter real GDP trend is under 1.5% - a K-shaped economy where profits take all the income growth

roster.name: Grantham
roster.note: latest sourced statement is June 2026 - inside the 6-month window but not fresh this fortnight
roster.statement_summary: Calls this 'the most expensive market in American history'; a reversion to trend would be closer to a wipeout than a correction, and the odds an AI bubble does not bust are 'slim to none'

roster.name: Burry
roster.note: THESIS BROADENED from AI/semis to housing and the credit cycle - which is why 36m goes to -3. His mortgage data is the real-economy version of what the HY tile is showing
roster.statement_summary: 'The Big Short is about to repeat itself': rates up six straight weeks, mortgage applications -6% w/w, purchase applications -14% y/y, refis -56% y/y, and serious 90+ day delinquencies up for the first time in five months, +19% y/y. Separately questions how fast Nvidia's AI chips lose economic value, citing the 1968 computer-financing cycle, and calls AI infrastructure commitments liabilities in 'hypergrowth mode'
